title: The Local 767 band marching in the Labor Day parade
summary: Marshall Royal's Local 767 band existed only for Los Angeles's Labor Day parade, in which Louis once played.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: What about the local 767 band -- circa 1939? Marshall Royal mentioned that and said that you were in it and that he conducted it.
That's when they used to march -- in the Labor Day parade. That's what that was.
The only time it played was just ...

Yeah, just on Labor Day. See, Labor Day in Los Angeles, they always had a big parade, you know, 10 or 15 different bands and Louis played in that with us one year. And everybody else used to ride on trucks because the musicians didn't want to walk that far, so they'd get the band on the trucks and they'd put the banners around the trucks.

But we walked, and it started at Peco and Broadway. That's where everybody backed up to -- Peco and Broadway and you started from Peco and Broadway, you go to City Hall, and that's where it would end. Now, that's quite ...
That's a little over a mile.
Yeah, that's quite a walk, you know.

But the same thing that I wrote for them to use the drum beat in that picture, that's what we used in that band, and we all walked this year, and it was nothing but a ba da dap da da da da ah da, you know, that type of thing.

And, so when we would start -- and you have to know when to start playing your music, see? You march and march because you're trying to blow the other bands out, and we did have good arrangements. We were playing things like "Christopher Columbus" and the other guys were playing Sousa's marches and those types of things, you know ... but we came in, you know, swinging!
As a matter of fact, Eddie Barefield made that arrangement for us on "Christopher Columbus". And all the best musicians in 767 would march on Labor Day.
Can you remember who all you marched with?
No. But I mean everybody in town

that could play at all, you know. I'm sure ... I know that Tyree did it, I know that Don Basas did it, and I know that Callender Eddie Barefield did it; I know Red Calendar did, because Red Callender Calendar is a very good tuba player, you know, and he was in it every year. And as you said, Marshall was in it, Marvin Johnson ...
Do you have a drum strapped on?

Uh huh. Yeah. We had about 5 snare drums and one bass drum, and Alton Redd-- Ni Redd's father played bass drum; you know, we made him play the bass drum because he's kind of a heavy set man, and we figured that he could take the whipping.
